title: Establish first-class Define ownership without authority collapse
outcome: Establish a source-backed, owner-qualified ontology contract in which the Define Project coordinates its product meaning, definition-routing boundary, and future locally owned model instance while preserving separate model, instance, definition, runtime, and adoption authority.
rationale: Define cannot become the semantic entry point for CyberAlchemy v2 by file placement or runtime success. Its durable Project identity and authority boundaries must exist before an exact recursive instance binding or runtime adoption can honestly be evaluated.
scope: a real CAV2-D60 Project identity for Define
one explicit Goal for first-class Define ownership and definition-routing semantics
exact candidate package identity and separately named owner routes
explicit residue for the missing inherited contract and adoption decision
a future D64 binding that can be evaluated only after its prerequisites exist
exclusions: automatic routing of live definition work
public Invoke migration, publication, release, deployment, or external effects
owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 definitions-governance owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 Define runtime owner

success_conditions.statement: Define has one schema-valid CAV2-D60 Project and one linked CAV2-D59 Goal whose identity and authority ceiling are source-backed.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: The Project and Goal close bidirectionally, cite the exact Define profile and candidate authority boundary, and retain authority_effect none.

success_conditions.statement: The proposed parent model and local Define instance have exact, separately scoped CAV2-D34 authority claims and one exact inherited contract.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: Owner-qualified model and instance authority-claim candidates plus a content-digested inherited-contract candidate bound to exact parent and instance profile states.

success_conditions.statement: The named adoption owner records an exact decision for the exact parent-model version and inherited contract.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: An owner decision record that states adoption posture, scope, version, challenge route, and authority effect without relying on Project membership or validation.

success_conditions.statement: A Project-owned RecursiveInstanceBinding closes every CAV2-D64 field and receives a review-only terminal evaluation without implying runtime enforcement.
success_conditions.evidence_requirement: A closed binding-registry entry, bidirectional Project reference, exact evidence refs, recursion stop, and GOV-RULE-D64-BINDING-COMPLETE evaluation.

evidence_requirements: Candidate package identity must remain distinct from adopted model identity.
Model, instance, definition, runtime, and adoption authority must remain separately scoped even when one actor fills more than one route.
Validation and Project membership must retain authority_effect none.
A binding may not be registered as satisfied until every D64 prerequisite resolves.

evidence_refs.claim_limit: Supports exact candidate package identity and declared owner routes only.
Supports the candidate separation of decision rights only; it is not an adoption decision.
Supports complete source-declared candidate claim tuples only; it does not activate either authority lane.
Supports exact candidate states and proposed mandatory terms only; it is not adoption or conformance.

revision_history.change: Created the proposed Define Project and its first ontology-only ownership Goal while preserving the empty D64 binding registry.
Added separate source-declared candidate model and instance authority tuples plus one exact-state inherited-contract candidate; adoption, conformance, and binding remain open.
revision_history.owner_route: CyberAlchemy v2 product owner plus CyberAlchemy v2 Define runtime owner

challenge_route: Challenge the Project or desired outcome through the product owner, canonical-definition implications through definitions governance, and any runtime or adoption interpretation through the Define runtime owner.
